title: The Day the Mississippi Ran Backward
topic: The Mississippi River ran backward (New Madrid earthquakes 1811-1812)
format_note: User-specified ~35 s historical Short with a user-given first line ('The Mississippi River once flowed backward.'), so it overrides the 50-60 s / 180-210 word targets and the He/It's/You opener on purpose (105 words, 34.2 s). The river is drawn far narrower than its real width so both banks read in a 9:16 frame.
mechanism: On 7 February 1812 the Reelfoot fault pushed up the land under the Mississippi like a step; the water piled against it, waterfalls formed and part of the current ran upstream for a few hours before flowing south again, while the sunken ground beside it filled to become Reelfoot Lake.

beats.hook: Brown water surges at the lens upstream past the NEW ORLEANS post; the boatman turns, shocked; a cottonwood smashes into the river
beats.story: A flatboat crew floating down to New Orleans past New Madrid, Missouri, the night the earthquakes strike
beats.rise: The boat rides the current south as usual; then cabins shake, chimneys fall, banks crack and crash into the water
beats.twist: Event: the land under the river pushes up like a giant step and the boat is carried back upstream
beats.mechanism: Labelled physical props: the riverbank slice with the LAND PUSHES UP block rising under the water, the NEW ORLEANS post with debris drifting the wrong way, the waterfall across the channel, the REELFOOT LAKE sign in the drowned forest
beats.ending: Dawn: the river runs south again; aerial over the changed land and the new lake; the last shot runs back into the opening surge (loop)
